scoring_justification: The porosity is computed from a full KMC simulation; recomputing it in the verifier would require re-running the expensive simulation, which is infeasible. Structural checks of monotonic trends and magnitude bounds derived from the paper's reported ranges faithfully verify the main claim.

hidden_assets.purpose: Porosity magnitude thresholds for NSD and composition sweeps
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper reports: porosity ~30% at low NSD (<1 nm⁻²), 3-7% at high NSD (>4 nm⁻²); pure Si porosity <4%, SiO₂ porosity ~15-20% (at NSD 1.74 nm⁻²). Thresholds set to porosity >0.2 at low NSD, <0.1 at high NSD, <0.05 at x=0, >0.1 at x=2.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Extracted from the qualitative statements in the paper.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: Derived directly from the paper's own reported ranges, ensuring a correct re-implementation can satisfy them.

outputs.description: Porosity and surface-to-volume ratio vs nucleation site density at fixed x=1.8
Porosity and surface-to-volume ratio vs oxygen composition at fixed NSD=1.74 nm⁻²

output_contract.notes: Both CSV files are scored by a hidden verifier that checks monotonic trends and absolute magnitude bounds without rerunning the simulation.

steps.description: Porosity must strictly decrease as nucleation site density (nsd_nm2) increases.
At the lowest tested NSD (<1 nm⁻²), porosity must exceed 0.2; at the highest tested NSD (>4 nm⁻²), porosity must be below 0.1.
Surface-to-volume ratio must strictly increase as nucleation site density increases.
Porosity must strictly increase as oxygen content x increases.
At x=0 porosity must be <0.05; at x=2 porosity must be >0.1.
Surface-to-volume ratio must be positive for all x values.
